final.investment_thesis:
All three risk seats, the Research Manager and the Trader converge on the same number — trim to 10% of total equity — and the disagreement is only about what would justify going back up, not about today's target. That consensus is earned by two pieces of evidence that survive every challenge. First, the tape has produced an actual failed push, not merely proximity to resistance: the 07-31 breakaway gap printed on 132.5M shares and remains unfilled ($311.80 high vs the $333.43 gap origin), the 08-03 session opened at $309.58 and was sold to $303.42 within $0.86 of the low, price is below the 50-SMA ($309.52), the 10-EMA ($322.91) and the VWMA ($325.09) — meaning the July buying cohort is underwater and supplies rallies — with MACD at 4.53 under its 7.51 signal and RSI 40.34 offering no oversold cushion. Reward to the first repair zone (~$309.5-$311.8, about +2%) against a ~9.8 ATR (~3.2%) is inverted, which is why I do not add at $303 and why the marginal share is worth more in cash. Second, the franchise is not impaired: Q3 FY26 revenue +16.4%, gross margin 50.06%, nine-month FCF $110.2B (+52.5%), ~$62B net cash, record Services, and the 200-SMA at $278.24 still beneath price. That asymmetry — broken short-term structure over an intact long-term business — is precisely the setup for Underweight rather than Sell.

This is where the prior lessons cut, and they cut in favor of trimming now. My repeated errors (2026-06-30, 07-01, 07-13, 07-21, 07-22, 07-23 Underweights) shared one failure mode: trimming on a sub-one-ATR close below a fast EMA while the 10-EMA > 50-SMA > 200-SMA stack was rising and MACD was still above signal. That gate — 'require an actual close below the 10-EMA/VWMA on expanding volume' — is now satisfied, and then some: the break came as a high-volume gap with price already beneath the 50-SMA, and the bounce attempt failed on the same session that opened at $309.58. The 2026-07-27 Hold was also wrong in the other direction: freezing at benchmark weight absorbed nearly the whole -9.9% five-day drawdown because no trim trigger was pre-committed alongside the additive ones. Repeating that here would mean holding 14.75% into a measured distribution with the event window (September guidance, input-cost commentary) still two-sided. The 08-03 entry at a $309.89 average cost is not an anchor: trimming 15.6 shares locks only ~$100 of realized loss plus ~$4.74 in fees, and the same-session failure of the entry thesis is fresh information, not a stale one. Cost basis informs the marginal sale, not the total target.

Sizing. The chosen 10% (~$9,969 / ~32.85 shares) is an independent total-exposure judgment. A concrete higher allocation of 15% (the current weight) would express confidence that the $303 area holds and that September guidance is benign — evidence I do not have, given an unfilled gap, a rejected bounce, and a company outlook the bear correctly describes as slower and more expensive; it would also leave no dry powder earmarked for the $294/$283.8 flush that the plan itself identifies as the better accumulation zone. A concrete lower allocation of 5% (or 0%) would treat a high-volume momentum break as a franchise break, forfeiting the ~1.5%-of-account contribution the retained core would earn on a V-recovery toward $350 and leaving 95-100% of the account in cash that earns nothing — a real cost, since AAPL has twice in eighteen months recovered this kind of gap within weeks. Downside on the chosen size: a slide to the $288.70 stop is about -4.9% on the sleeve, or roughly -0.5% of total equity; to the $278.24 200-SMA, about -8.3% on the sleeve, or ~-0.8% of equity. Upside: a repair through $322.9-$325.1 and the gap-fill at $333.4 toward $340-$350 is +6% to +15% on the sleeve, ~+0.6% to +1.5% of equity. I am not assigning probabilities to those paths — the evidence does not calibrate them — but the retained 10% is the size at which the cash-opportunity cost and the downside loss are both tolerable, and neither argument auto-overrides the other.

What would change the call: restoring toward 12-15% only on a volume-backed close above $309.5-$311.8 (reclaiming the 50-SMA and breaking the failed-bounce pattern), or after a flush into $294 and then $283.8 that stabilizes on contracting volume — both narrative conditions, not implemented orders. Further reduction toward 5% or below on a close under $278.24, which would invalidate the structural thesis, or on September guidance showing sequential margin compression with a quantified component/memory cost hit. Explicit gaps, not papered over: no actual September-quarter guidance figures, no quantified component/memory cost, no AI roadmap detail, no consensus estimates or valuation multiple, and no options-implied move — so the $325 reference is a technical repair zone, not a valuation-derived target; the fundamentals cited are the most recent filing, not forward numbers.
